content.comment_body: Hello experts. I have a question about connecting a three-wire pressure transducer (atlas copco [article_no]) with a 0.5-4.5V range to the [product_name] analog input (0-10V). The transducer has Signal, GND, and V+ wires. I've tried several wiring methods, but the analog value never increases along with the pressure shown on the manometer.

You haven't specified the sensor's voltage supply value. If your supply is 24 VDC, you can use the [product_name]. Otherwise, you should connect the GND from the sensor supply to the GND (0V) of the [product_name] so both reference potentials are the same.
Thank you for your interest in my question. The sensor requires a 5VDC supply, so I believe I need an external power source. What is the best way to connect the sensor after that?

You will need an external power supply for the sensor. A simple voltage stabilizer IC (Type 7805, approx. 1 Euro) should work. Connect 5V+ from the supply to the sensor's V+, the sensor's signal output to the [product_name] analog input, and 5V- (GND) to the sensor's GND. Make sure to connect 5V GND to the minus (M) terminal of the [product_name] power. Note, you must have a DC version if you want to use analog input on the basic module. Since the input works from 0-10V and the sensor outputs 0.5-4.5V, the measurement resolution will be less than half the normal—typically, the resolution for 10V is 1000, so for 4V, it's about 400. Good luck.
Thank you very much. Could you please help me improve the program from this thread: [url] so I can use it with my 0.5-4.5V sensor? I'm new to [product_name] programming and find it difficult.
What is the sensor's pressure range and which [product_name] module are you using?
The sensor range is 0-10 bar and the [product_name] I have is [article_no].

You need to perform some calculations. With a sensor output of 0.5V-4.5V (4V span) and the [product_name] working in the 0-10V range, consider: 0.5V to 4.5V equals 4V for 0-10 bar. If the input span were 10V, it would cover 25 bar (10/4 x 10). Since the sensor starts at 0.5V, not 0V, the offset is 1.25 bar (0.5V in a 25 bar range). So, sensor offset = -1.25 bar; end range = 23.75 bar. Set your analog amplifier block accordingly.
